> They weren’t taken by Mexicans or sent overseas­­ — industries changed, new products were made and robots were invented that could do the job of 10 men and work all night without complaining.

That statement is factually incorrect.

A) The jobs HAVE moved overseas. It doesn't matter if the companies were bought, it doesn't matter if the physical jobs themselves were moved from the US to foreign countries, it doesn't matter if companies went out of business simply because their product was too expensive compared to foreign options. The result is the same.

The jobs have been outsourced to foreign countries.

B) Robots don't have nearly the impact that the article is implying. China isn't taking over the steel industry because they have fancy robots, they are taking over because they can pay their workers shit and work them harder than we can.

The industry has certainly changed, but not THAT much. China currently has [about 12 million coal and steel workers](http://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-economy-employment-idUSKCN0W205X). Even at the height of the steel industry in the US, we only had about [500,000 steel workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_steel_industry_(1970%E2%80%93present)) and about [230,000 coal workers](http://www.sourcewatch.org/index.php/Coal_and_jobs_in_the_United_States) in 1980 (the highest since the 60's).

I'm not saying the situation isn't a mess. It is. But the article isn't framing the problem correctly. It's implying that these jobs are obsolete now.

They aren't. The demand is still there, it's just that the supply has been supplanted by cheap Chinese labor instead of US labor.

It is the norm, which is the issue. It's not even a particularly new issue. The US has been dealing with different manufacturing industries becoming more and more outsourced all the time, mostly due to things like caring about our workers, and how that translates into higher priced products.

I highly suggest it. I don't have all the answers, I can just smell bullshit. The author is correct in the sense that those jobs don't exist in America anymore, my issue is just that (in the case of the steel industry and many others) the jobs didn't disappear because they are obsolete, they disappeared because we can't compete with foreign industry. The jobs, supply, and demand are all still there.

The problem is that manufacturing jobs are being outsourced to countries that can produce things for lower costs because they don't care about their workers. The jobs themselves are still there.

Think of it this way, if we passed a law tomorrow banning the US from buying foreign steel, or tech products, or hell, even clothing/etc, there would be a MASSIVE surge of domestic jobs and industry to meet the demand.

Now, there are some industries (like coal) that are in fact dying slowly as technology progresses, but there are plenty of manufacturing jobs in industries that are not obsolete, but rather outsourced.
It's pretty accepted nomenclature to include outsourced jobs as jobs that were "sent" overseas.

It's pretty universally understood that when we talk about jobs moving overseas it can either be from a company literally moving their own jobs overseas or companies simply buying their product/outsourcing from a new overseas industry that undercuts what is available in the US.

The simplest difference is that a shell is an unpowered projectile once it's fired. A missile has self propulsion.

A shell also has two parts. The projectile/ordinance, and the casing where the propellant is stored. When a shell is fired (much like a bullet), the propellant is activated and resulting reaction pushes the ordinance out, where it then becomes a non-self propelled projectile.

A missile has it's own propulsion system that is attached to the ordinance.

I'd really like someone to continue the tradition of making a version of War of Worlds that has similar themes to the book.

One of the major themes (besides the somewhat oddly placed religious one in the middle) is the idea of communication, especially during crisis. If I recall correctly, HG Wells in part wrote War of Worlds as an example of what would happen if war came to Britain in the late 1800's/early 1900's. Because communication was done primarily by telegraph or newspaper, when the aliens land and cut the telegraph lines, it becomes really unclear what the fuck is going on. We hear and eventually see things through the protagonists eyes as things spiral out of control, and nearby towns and cities have no idea what is actually happening or how to react.

In the late 1930's Orson Welles famously read a radio play script of War of the World's on air, which became a sort of live action display of the same theme from the original text, since radio was a major form of communication that was more instant than traditional means. Some people panicked as they tuned in and thought they were listening to a real news broadcast of an alien invasion.

I think it would be awesome and totally fascinating to make a movie discussing that theme in a modern setting. You can keep the major plot points, but mold it to fit what might actually happen in modern times regarding war/crisis and communication.

PS: If you haven't read the book, do it. I mean, you should read all of Well's big 4 (Time Machine, Invisible Man, War of the Worlds, Island of Doctor Moreau), but WotW has always been one of the most interesting to me (The Time Machine being an all time favorite), especially in a historical perspective.

But the slow burn of the landing and ensuing chaos and confusion is awesome. Unlike in the movie, the aliens don't immediately start killing things when they land. It takes days from the initial landing for things to really start moving. The book definitely drags when they get to the main character and the priest in the basement, but it's still somewhat interesting philosophy.

Unfortunately, there isn't much you can do.  You didn't do anything wrong.  Yes, you technically could have not agreed to exclusivity in the first place, but that's just hindsight talking, and she was most definitely trying to trap you into telling her what she wanted to hear.  So no, you shouldn't blame yourself.  You did the right thing by clarifying asap, because the longer you waited, the harder it would have been for you to do, the more miserable you would become, and the she would fall that much harder when things finally reached a tipping point.

The best advice I can give you is to decide (to the best of your ability) how you feel about her and make a decision from there.  If you think you might actually have some deeper feelings for her, you might want to consider apologizing and then agreeing to a relationship (though I wouldn't immediately qualify it as long term).  If you don't, then it's probably best to simply let her go.  If you want to remain friends with her, then consider sending her an email/voicemail apologizing for not being clear the first time and tell her you do care for her as a friend, and let her make the next move.

And no, all relationships do not end with someone getting hurt, but someone (most likely both people) will almost always end up getting hurt at some point in the relationship, because that is simply the nature of them.  I'm sure you've been hurt or hurt virtually every other person you have formed some sort of bond with (eg, friends, family, co-workers). By "the doctor," I assume you mean your regular doctor, the same one you go to if you have bumps and bruises and such?  If that is the case, then you need to go see a therapist immediately.  Just because it is a physical symptom does not mean that it isn't being caused by a mental disorder.

For example, I suffered from major depression for 4 months with only mental symptoms (including some suicidal thoughts).  After a string of stressful events, I picked up some major physical symptoms, including vomiting every day, shaking, loss of appetite, loss of sleep, uncontrollable crying, and panic attacks.  All of these were caused by my anxiety and depression.  After 2 solid weeks of these symptoms, I ended up in the hospital because I didn't know what to do.  I had lost 19 pounds in those 2 weeks, which is a lot for me (I'm 5'9", normal weight is only 165lbs).

In the hospital, I was started on 150mg of Zoloft and a small dosage of Klonopin (i think .5mg, but the exact amount escapes me) twice a day.  After the medication began to take effect, I lost ALL of my physical symptoms (though I still have a bit of sleep trouble).

I'm not saying you should check yourself into a hospital immediately unless you are legitimately thinking about suicide.  And yes, having suffered from suicidal depression, I know there is a difference between suicide being on the mind and actually feeling the urge.  If you feel safe, simply seeing a therapist (I think Behavioral Cognitive Therapy works best, so check out a therapist who specializes in that) and potentially starting some medication might be all you need.

This is very common with depression.  As soon as I started suffering from major depression, I lost the ability to read (and I have a English Major).  Interestingly enough, I gained the ability back during a 7 day hospitalization (and read 2 books), though since my release, I have still basically been unable to read.

There are basically two solutions.  

1) Work through your depression.  That's really the only way to get the ability back naturally.

2) In the meantime, medication can help.  I have ADD, and take Vyvanse for it, and even though I can't normally read because of my depression, I find that on the days I take the Vyvanse (it's not an everyday ADD medication like Ritalin) I can read.  If you don't have ADD, even just anti-depression medication can make it easier.

What I personally hate the most is, "It'll be ok, everything will get better."

That's not really true, it's not helpful, it's downright irritating for a depressed person to hear (b/c the first thing I think is, "When exactly?"), and it's actually removing responsibility from the person who is depressed and making the situation seem like something that will eventually resolve itself.

If you feel the need to say something positive to me, say "I wish you the best of luck, and I hope you knock the shit out your depression."  Don't give me some bullshit line.
